decision.rationale: Only one non-excluded direct-match candidate is visible in the provided list: PGS002790. It is concept-aligned at trait_reported/trait_efo (autism spectrum disorder) and evaluated in EUR, but has weaker endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported = 'Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)') and modest PRS contribution (partial R²≈0.00546; full_model_r2 reported, no PGS-only AUC/R², no effect sizes). With no other eligible candidates shown, it is the sole supportable runner-up and is repeated to satisfy the required two-element runners_up schema.

From the remaining visible candidates (PGS002787, PGS002788), both are same-publication SDPR genome-wide scores with identical EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry and the same basic covariates (age, PCs1-3), so endpoint fidelity and transportability are broadly comparable. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2; the only comparable metric available is the selected record’s partial R² (full_model_r2). PGS002788 has the highest partial R² (0.00307 vs 0.00275), with similar validation size (n=2,524 vs n=2,198) and similar variant counts, so it is the stronger-supported runner-up. PGS002787 is the only other supportable runner-up in the candidate list.

Among the remaining direct-match candidates, PGS000704 is the strongest runner-up on structural and evidence breadth: it targets the same EFO trait, uses a genome-wide snpnet multi-PRS approach with very large variant count (183,271) and large UKB development (n=223,327), and reports a time-to-event discrimination metric (C-index 0.711) with only basic covariates (age as timescale, sex, batch, PCs), avoiding heavy clinical packaging. PGS001777 is the next-best supported: it is also an exact EFO match and disease-focused (alcohol-related cirrhosis in drinkers), reports AUROC 0.671 and a strong stratification effect (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18), but is a very sparse 3-variant score with unknown covariates and much smaller validation (n=1,390), making it less robust than PGS000704.

Among remaining direct-match celiac disease candidates, PGS000040 has the strongest reported discrimination signal (AUROC=0.90 in European evaluation) with a disease-focused publication and a clean, specific endpoint (“Coeliac disease”), making it the best-supported runner-up despite only full-model AUROC being available. For the second runner-up, PGS001301 provides the clearest PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.8287; PGS-only R2=0.1422) with standard demographic/PC covariates and large UKB training, offering stronger standalone-PRS evidence than other alternatives that lack PRS-only metrics (the UKB portability scores report only partial-r; PGS004930 has lower AUROC=0.67; PGS000041/042 are restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers and have lower AUROC ~0.72–0.73).

With PGS001033 excluded, only two candidates remain in the visible list, both targeting the same closely related endpoint (congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency / congenital deficiency of other clotting factors including factor VII) and coming from the same UKB portability framework paper with identical training size (n=391,124), evaluation ancestry mix (EUR/SAS), covariates, and essentially identical partial-correlation performance (partial-r ~0.056). Between them, PGS002034 is mildly preferred as the runner-up #1 due to stronger methodological/structural signals (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 32,552 variants vs penalized regression with 45 variants), which is the recommended tie-break when endpoint and reported metrics are effectively indistinguishable. PGS001826 is the remaining supportable runner-up #2.

Among remaining candidates, PGS001339 is the closest endpoint match with comparable, PRS-only metrics reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.613; PGS-only R2=0.02447) and the same clean/basic covariate set as the excluded primary (age, sex, array, PCs). Although its phenotyping is time-to-event AF+flutter (slightly broader and TTE), it still explicitly includes atrial flutter and provides directly comparable PRS-only performance evidence, which is stronger support than candidates lacking PRS-only AUC/R2. Between the two portability-study options (PGS001841 vs PGS002050), both share the same endpoint/covariates/training context and report only partial correlation (no PRS-only AUROC/R2); PGS002050 is marginally better supported due to slightly higher partial-r (0.1034 vs 0.1026) and a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) that is structurally favored over a sparser penalized regression when other evidence is otherwise tied.

Among remaining direct-match AAA scores, PGS001784 has the cleanest PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports a covariates-regressed-out (PGS-only) Nagelkerke R2=0.014661 in EUR evaluation (n=350,767) using a strong genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant count, and the R2 is plausible under the local h2_liability ceiling (~0.02). For the second runner-up, PGS002054 provides PRS-comparable signal via partial correlation (partial-r=0.0144) from a large UKB-derived LDpred2 genome-wide score (592k variants) with multi-ancestry evaluation records; while it lacks explicit PGS-only R2/AUC, its structural method/variant profile and comparable metric support are stronger than alternatives that report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates (PGS003429/PGS003972) or a likely covariate-driven high C-index without PRS-only metrics (PGS003973).

From the visible candidate list (PGS000924, PGS001824, PGS002032), excluding the primary pick PGS002032 leaves PGS001824 and PGS000924 as the only eligible runners-up. Ranked by direct-match support: (1) PGS001824 is an exact endpoint match to the target (trait_efo bilirubin metabolism disease; phenotyping_reported Disorders of bilirubin excretion) and is a same-publication sibling of the excluded model with identical partial-r evidence (partial-r=0.0716) and similar multi-ancestry evaluation context; despite missing PRS-only AUC/R2, it remains the closest, most coherent direct-match alternative. (2) PGS000924 is a broader but still relevant endpoint (porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism disorders, time-to-event) with explicit PRS-only metrics reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.88697; PGS-only R2=0.21843) and basic covariates; however it comes from a pan-trait UKB sparse framework (snpnet, 5 variants) and uses a time-to-event phenotype, both of which reduce confidence versus the exact bilirubin-excretion endpoint.

Ranked runners-up emphasize endpoint fidelity plus the strongest PRS-comparable evidence available after excluding PGS004546. (1) PGS001174 is a direct cholelithiasis model with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.623, PGS-only R2=0.028) and basic covariates; its PRS-only R2 is plausible relative to the EUR h2_obs ceiling (~0.021–0.029) and it has multi-ancestry evaluation, making it the cleanest, most comparable performance-supported alternative. (2) PGS002072 targets a very close composite endpoint (cholelithiasis and cholecystitis) and reports a slightly stronger PRS-comparable partial correlation (partial-r=0.098 vs 0.0948 for its sibling PGS001861) with large UKB training (n=391,124) and multi-ancestry evaluation; despite lacking AUROC/R2, it is better supported than PGS004476 (unknown covariates, only OR=1.22) and PGS005150 (EAS-only evaluation and only beta effect size, less aligned to general deployment).

From the remaining visible candidates (PGS000201, PGS000202, PGS002739), all have acceptable endpoint alignment to alcohol dependence/AUD, but differ in strength of reported PRS contribution and transportability context. PGS000201 is the strongest runner-up: it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (~1.09M), has a reasonably sized EUR evaluation (n=7,599), and reports the largest PRS incremental signal among the two sibling problematic-alcohol-use scores (ΔR²=0.01192 vs 0.00456 for PGS000202), with standard/basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array/site). PGS002739 is the next best-supported: it is a direct AUD endpoint and reports a meaningful discrimination effect size (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.76) in an AFR evaluation cohort (n=6,315), providing complementary ancestry evidence versus the EUR-only PGS000201/202; however it is gene-based with very low variant count (858) and unknown covariates, so it ranks below PGS000201. PGS000202 is deprioritized as a weaker near-clone of PGS000201 with smaller validation (n=1,251) and smaller incremental ΔR².

Among remaining direct-match cervical cancer/cervical carcinoma candidates, PGS000073 and PGS000784 have the strongest endpoint fidelity (both explicitly "Incident cervical cancer") and coherent evaluation context (EUR validation in a large cohort, n=211,795). Their reported discrimination is similar (full-model AUROC ~0.745; C-index ~0.75) with moderate per-SD HRs (~1.21–1.22), and covariates are standard epidemiologic/demographic adjustments (age, PCs/array, smoking pack-years plus reproductive factors), avoiding heavy clinical leakage. By contrast, PGS001299 is a pan-trait UKB sparse framework score with very weak PRS-only signal (PGS-only AUROC 0.552; PGS R2 0.00263), PGS003389 shows weak full-model AUROC (0.563) and minimal R2, and PGS005165 is EAS-only (less ancestry-compatible if EUR deployment is assumed) with similarly modest C-index (0.566). Therefore the best-supported runners-up are the Graff et al. 10-variant score (PGS000073) and its closely matched inverse-weight variant (PGS000784).

With the exact-label UKB snpnet framework score (PGS001135) excluded, the strongest remaining direct matches to the same broad endpoint (arthritis; not a specific subtype like RA, OA, gout, JIA) are the two Commun Biol “Integration of risk factor PRS with disease PRS” models that explicitly target EFO:arthritis via the same phenotype family: PGS004477 (LDpred2; M13 Other arthritis) and PGS004547 (RFDiseasemetaPRS; M13 Other arthritis). Both are EUR DEV/EVAL, have substantial UKB-based training (n=174,489) and coherent phenotype alignment to the target trait, unlike the many higher-AUC candidates that are for different arthritis entities (e.g., ankylosing spondylitis, RA, OA, gout) and thus are weaker endpoint matches for generic ‘arthritis’. Between the two, both have limited comparable performance reporting (only ORs; covariates unknown), but they remain the best-supported runners-up because they preserve endpoint fidelity to arthritis itself; PGS004547 has a slightly higher reported OR (1.262 vs 1.196), while PGS004477 uses a standard genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2).

Among the remaining direct-match basal cell carcinoma PRSs, the strongest support comes from the same Cancer PRSweb (Am J Hum Genet 2020) family with identical endpoint/covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4; EUR dev/eval), so differences in full-model AUROC/OR are more comparable within-family. PGS000454 (P+T, 27 variants) is essentially tied with the excluded primary on full-model AUROC (0.632 with identical CI bounds) and has the highest/near-highest reported Nagelkerke R² in the pool (0.0489) plus strong top-1% vs rest OR (3.79), making it the closest-supported sibling alternative. For the second runner-up, PGS000456 (GWAS Hits, 30 variants) has nearly the same full-model AUROC (0.630) and similarly strong effect sizes (per-SD OR 1.633; top-1% vs rest OR 3.95) with the same clean covariate set and endpoint fidelity, outperforming other siblings with materially lower AUROC/R² (e.g., PGS000445–451) and avoiding the weaker-evidence candidates with unknown covariates or missing discrimination metrics.

Top runners-up prioritize endpoint fidelity to generic atopic eczema/dermatitis and PRS-relevant evidence while avoiding therapy-specific paradoxical-eczema endpoints. PGS004587 is a direct-match incident atopic dermatitis endpoint with a reported HR (1.153, 95% CI 1.037–1.282) and very large EUR evaluation (n=337,910); despite being GWAS-hits (23 variants) and lacking PRS-only AUC/R2, it has clean phenotype alignment and comparable time-to-event effect-size evidence. PGS001773 has a more restricted endpoint (moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in Canadian cohorts) and its very high full-model AUROC/R2 (0.93/0.49) is likely covariate-influenced (age/sex/parental ethnicity) and not PRS-only, but it remains disease-focused with a direct AD endpoint and avoids the paradoxical-eczema treatment-context mismatch seen in PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903.

Among remaining candidates, the strongest direct-match support comes from the same aortic-stenosis publication family with endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported = incident aortic stenosis and clean/basic covariates (age/age^2/sex/PCs). PGS005254 is the closest sibling to the excluded primary: exact trait_reported aortic stenosis, PRS-CS genome-wide shrinkage with ~1.11M variants, and a strong per-SD effect size (HR=1.64, 95% CI 1.50–1.78) in a large EUR evaluation (n=244,450). For the second runner-up, PGS005255 edges PGS005256 because it has the same incident aortic stenosis endpoint/covariates/publication and similar genome-wide PRS-CS construction, but shows a slightly stronger HR (1.53, CI 1.40–1.66) than PGS005256 (1.53, CI 1.41–1.67) and is tied on evaluation context; both are still direct-match via phenotyping_reported despite trait_reported being valve-function measurements. The hypertrophic cardiomyopathy scores (PGS000739/PGS000778/PGS004910/PGS004911) are deprioritized due to phenotype mismatch to aortic stenosis despite some reporting higher full-model AUROC, which is not PRS-comparable and is secondary to endpoint fidelity.

With PGS002089 excluded, the strongest remaining direct-match evidence comes from the two snpnet UK Biobank models that report explicit PRS-comparable (PGS-only) discrimination metrics with basic covariates and large validation. PGS001268 (time-to-event AS) has slightly stronger PRS-only AUROC (0.7346 vs 0.7265) and PRS-only R2 (0.1023 vs 0.0988) than PGS001267, with similar endpoint alignment to ankylosing spondylitis and comparable covariate cleanliness (age/sex/array/PCs). The other candidates either lack PRS-only metrics entirely (PGS001876 only partial-r; Taiwanese EAS models report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and small n=1,298), making them less directly supported for standalone PRS ranking under the provided policy.

Only two direct-match candidates are visible for corneal dystrophy, and the primary pick excludes PGS002042. The remaining candidate PGS001835 is endpoint-faithful (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all corneal dystrophy), from the same publication family and cohort context (UKB portability study; DEV EUR with multi-ancestry EVAL), with basic demographic/PC covariates (sex, age, birth date, deprivation index, 16 PCs) and a reported PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation partial-r=0.0384, EUR validation). No other candidates remain, so PGS001835 is repeated to satisfy the required two-element runners_up list.
